subject: Sampling guidance + cost-mapping tiles for Console (actionable ask)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sampling guidance + cost-mapping tiles for Console (actionable ask)

Team,

Quick background: we've had multiple customer reports (Acme Health among them) where per-route alerts and billing export numbers don't match our console's top-line cost for tenant trials. The root cause in a number of cases looks like sampling (route-level live sampling + prefix/KV cache interactions) and the way we expose rate-adjusted token counts in the UI.

Requests (priority: high for this cycle — customer demo week of Oct 11):
- Add a visible sampling-rate indicator on each route row (and route detail) that shows the current sample rate and the timestamp when that sample rate was last computed.
- Add an "Estimated cost (adjusted)" metric that applies the sampling multiplier to the token count so sales/CS can reconcile bill estimates with sampled metrics. This should be exportable in billing CSVs.
- Provide a small tile on Console home (per-tenant) summarizing: active sampled routes, avg sample rate (last 24h), and an estimated delta vs unsampled cost.
- Add an admin toggle to override sampling window for an endpoint (30m/2h/24h) for debugging and for canary customers.

Deliverables I'd like by EOW Oct 7 (engineering + product): prototype tiles + data contract, an approach doc for how sampling interacts with KV cache and batching, and a short runbook for CS to use when customers hit unexpected bills.

I've attached a short proposal (sampling-proposal.pdf) and two quick mock images (mock_tiles.png) to show suggested placement.

Why this matters: until we present numbers that clearly adjust for sampling, CS/sales are forced to over-provision credits or spend time manually reconciling exports. This is a repeatable ops cost and a demo risk for large trial customers.

Questions from me: can infra provide a streaming endpoint that emits per-route effective sample rate at ~1m granularity? If not, what would be the cheapest approximation?

Thanks — Tessa

-- 
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sampling guidance + cost-mapping tiles for Console (actionable ask)

Tessa — thanks for the write-up and the mocks. Quick thoughts:

- We can emit an "effective_sample_rate" counter from the runtime, but it will be an approximation in earliest iterations (based on request sampling logs and batch sizes). True 1m granularity will require a small telemetry pipeline change.
- Important callout: changing sampling window in prod to very small windows could cause churn in our billing metrics and might trigger false positives in alerting. We need to ensure SLOs are not impacted by surface-level sampling toggles.

Can you drop the telemetry ID / existing dashboard or the historical query you use for the 24h avg? That'll help us size the infra change (and whether we can do an on-demand aggregation vs a continuous stream).

I'll carve out time with Infra to outline the delta for OBS-8421 — if anyone on this thread already has an existing query, paste it here.

-Markus

Subject: Re: Sampling guidance + cost-mapping tiles for Console (actionable ask)

Thanks Tessa — this is actionable and aligns with things we've been sketching. A couple practical proposals for how to break this down so teams can take clear ownership:

1) Data-first incremental approach (Infra): add a lightweight counter stream named "route_effective_sample_rate" with minute-ish buckets that records (route_id, tenant_id, sample_rate, sample_window_sec). Start by storing the last 6h in Redis and rolling up to ClickHouse for historicals. This should be low cost and supports the tile.

2) UX-first minimal surface (Product + DX):
   - Phase 1: read-only sampling indicator on route row + hover that shows sample_rate and last_seen.
   - Phase 2: add an "Estimated cost (adjusted)" column in per-route table and allow CSV export that includes both sampled and adjusted numbers.

3) Runbook (CS): a short doc for CS to quickly reconcile billing exports vs Console (link below).

I've created a short design stub and added it to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfG-sample-rate-guidelines

For the SLO concern Markus raised: we should gate the admin override behind an internal feature flag and include a warning if the window is changed within the last 24h. Also, we should make the override a non-persistent view (i.e., it affects only the displayed calculations unless explicitly applied).

Attachments: sampling-proposal.pdf, mock_tiles.png

- Grace

Hi Tessa / Grace — thanks for looping us in. We're one of the tenants who saw a ~3x delta last week between the trial dashboard estimate and the CSV export. Anything you can do to surface the sampling rate and an adjusted estimate will make it much easier for our billing team to forecast.

Small ask from our side: if you build the admin override, can you also expose a short API endpoint (or export column) that indicates whether an override was in effect during the billing window? That would help our audit team reconcile chargebacks.

Happy to join a quick call if it's helpful.

— Julie
Customer Success Manager
Acme Health
